peer_matches.query_passage:
The community bakery discards unsold bread at closing, but baking less every day could leave weekend customers empty handed. I propose a two colour chalkboard tally of early and late sales. The baker can record loaves by product without linking purchases to individual customers. After a fortnight, dough batches for slow weekday afternoons can be reduced while weekend production remains unchanged.

Weather and a neighbouring school holiday could distort the short trial, so the tally should include those circumstances in a margin note. Donating edible leftovers must remain an option while production is adjusted. A reduction in waste accompanied by repeated stockouts would count as failure, because discarded weight alone rewards underproduction. The baker should compare both leftovers and unfilled requests before continuing. Feedback can come from a small basket of paper comments near the counter. The proposed intervention is a production scheduling change that uses equipment already present in the shop

exclusions.passage: Riverton University invites teams to design a practical improvement for a small community institution. The institution has limited money, uncertain demand, and a responsibility to serve residents fairly. Your proposal should identify one operational problem, explain why existing practices are inadequate, and recommend an intervention that can be tested within one academic term. State the assumptions behind your analysis and explain which observations would cause you to change your recommendation. Include a way to measure progress without collecting unnecessary personal information. Discuss an implementation risk, a possible unintended consequence, and a low cost method for gathering feedback. The evaluation panel values clear reasoning over ambitious technology. Teams may use simple schedules, physical tools, or public information where appropriate. Do not assume that additional staff, permanent subsidies, or expensive equipment will become available. Conclude by explaining how the institution could decide whether to continue, adapt, or stop the proposed pilot after review

ai_indicator.explanation: Weighted style regularity/repetition/transition index. Not a calibrated probability or proof of AI authorship. Synthetic AI labels do not establish detector validity.

scoring.percentage_formula: 100 * union of query word positions in accepted windows / eligible query words
scoring.coverage_caveat: Coverage of candidate semantic windows; can include unmatched context. Not percentage proven plagiarized. Peer and external percentages are separate, not additive.
scoring.risk_rule: HIGH coverage >=50%; MEDIUM >=15%; else LOW. AI indicator never raises risk alone.
scoring.unknown_rule: Unassessable and fully excluded documents have null scores; partial PDFs cover extracted text only.
